## Reactive intermediates in biocatalytic processes

Characterising short-lived, highly reactive intermediates in enzyme active sites, and using that control to unlock transformations enzymes do not perform in nature. Carbene and nitrene transfer, radical relay chemistry in nonheme iron enzymes, and selective oxidations.

::: {.cbc-side-label}

## Multiscale protocols in biocatalysis

Integrating QM, QM/MM, molecular dynamics, enhanced sampling and electrostatic analysis into workflows that connect conformational dynamics with chemical reactivity. Method development as much as application: understanding where current protocols break down when applied to biochemical systems.

::: {.cbc-side-label}

## Biochemical mechanisms

Reconstructing how biomolecular processes evolve in time, and how their environment reshapes them — protonation states, pH, ligand binding, crowding. Long-timescale processes such as millisecond allosteric activation.

::: {.cbc-side-label}

## Supramolecular processes

Host–guest recognition, encapsulation and regioselective reactivity in adaptable cages, capsules and supramolecular masks, largely in collaboration with the Ribas group at IQCC.
